findings.finding: The unit spec still requires Q1 (tag after merge), Q3 (refuse concurrent hand-run), an FR-01.09 amendment, and a `--promise-only --repin` for changed promise tests. The diff implements none of these, and D82(1) admits the spec file was never amended. The re-scope is an operator decision in a chat, recorded only in FINDINGS.
findings.suggestion: Have the orchestrator amend or annotate the P8a spec file before stop 3, so the AC record (`changed`/`unchanged` per §3a) is auditable against a written spec rather than a FINDINGS paragraph.

findings.finding: The promise list changed, but the diff contains no `promise.lock.json` delta and no `--promise-only --repin` output, which the freeze rules require when a promise test moves. If `promise.lock.json` pins `promise_list.json`, `golden_lock.py --check` should fail; if it doesn't, the spec's promise-lock step silently doesn't apply.
findings.suggestion: Run `golden_lock.py --promise-only --repin` (or show that the lock does not cover these entries) and add the before/after delta; name the promise tests in the PR as the spec asks.

findings.finding: The replay driver's trunk lookup neither uses `--end-of-options` nor the `_BRANCH` sanitisation that `release_event.trunk()` applies. A default branch name starting with `-` (or any name failing the regex) is accepted in the replay driver and fed into `--base`, so the replay and the real CLI disagree on the exact input F5 is about.

prepare` now always runs two remote git calls (`remote get-url --push`, `ls-remote --symref`) with the runner's default 600 s timeout and without `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`; an unreachable or credential-prompting remote stalls every `prepare` and every `record-event` on a pre-F5 run state. D82(3) records this as "open", but it is a new production stall path introduced by this unit (the closing verify's fetch at least runs only at the end).
findings.suggestion: Set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and a short timeout on these two calls now; a `--no-network` fallback or hard failure can stay a follow-up.

findings.finding: release_flow` runs the preview step and then the real `aggregate` unconditionally; a `cancel` outcome from the preview step would still write. The Cancel-leaves-no-trace behaviour is proven only by the bespoke S18a flow, so the shared flow used by ~30 other guided scenarios would not catch a regression where Cancel no longer stops the write.
findings.suggestion: In `release_flow`, return early when the preview result's choice is `cancel` (mirroring SKILL Step 5), so every guided scenario exercises the branch.

findings.finding: The PR base is asserted as the literal `"main"` rather than read from the remote/trunk the scenario just established; the test claims to prove F5 but would pass if the base were hard-coded back to `main` in a repo whose default is `main`. Only S14c (a `master` repo) actually proves the dynamic base, and it has no PR at all.
findings.suggestion: Assert `pr["base"] == driver.trunk(scratch)` (or add a `master`-default repo with a feature-branch release asserting `base == "master"`).

findings.finding: _BRANCH` accepts names containing `..`, a trailing `/` or `.lock`, and a trailing `.` — git rejects these as branch names but they pass the guard and land in a push line / `--base`.
findings.suggestion: Tighten the regex (reject `..`, `.lock` suffix, trailing `.` and `/`), or keep as-is and note it; low real-world risk since the value comes from the remote.  Positives worth noting: `--no-follow-tags` on both head pushes closes a real tag-leak hole (D81); `on_base` now prefers the stored `trunk` over re-asking `origin/HEAD`, fixing the carried-over P4 review item; the escape-budget drop to 0 is correctly pinned in the hardening test; the approved_deltas list covers every changed frozen file I can see.  Overall: ship-with-fixes — the behaviour changes themselves are sound and well tested; the promise-lock handling, the replay/CLI trunk-parsing divergence, and the unsanitised network lookup in `prepare` should be settled (or explicitly waived in FINDINGS) before stop 3.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: Edit requires a drop file, but `prepare` now deliberately defers upgrade-note drops while preview confirmation is pending. The preview can therefore contain an upgrade note with no file to edit, and the real aggregation creates and renders it only after acceptance. FINDINGS D82 acknowledges this unresolved path.
findings.suggestion: Support editing the pending upgrade-note representation before acceptance and ensure the repeated dry run renders that edited text without creating repository files.

findings.finding: The diff approves new hashes for numerous regenerated traces, beginning with `S1.drops.trace.json`, but includes no corresponding trace-file changes. With the supplied diff, the approved `after` hashes cannot match those files, so the golden check cannot validate the declared regeneration.
